endings.author: Truth
dedications:
For my grandmother,
who knew who I was.

For the baker’s son,
who went off to read.

For Mum,
who called me from the door.

For my grandmother,
who was right.

For whoever wrote in the margins,
and does not remember.

For the caretaker,
who noticed nothing.
blurbs: “A chipped cup. A key never returned. A voice, at night, on the edge of the bed.”
Before the Library, there was a childhood. The first volume of The Story of Babel.
“No one said its name. They said: over there.”
A rumour. People who never come back. A library that does not exist.
“It was not there the day before.”
A door at the end of a hallway known by heart. All it took was to open it.
“Hexagons. More hexagons. And books, everywhere.”
The first day in the Library. Then all the others.
“Everyone says there is no way out.”
There is a path. You only have to accept what it costs.
“The coffee tasted the same. The street sounded the same.”
Coming back. Taking your place again. Pretending.
“I see it as soon as I close my eyes.”
The shelves come back at night. Then by day.
“This time, I knew where the door was.”
Going back where no one returns from. A second time.
“Somewhere, a book holds the answer. I never knew the question.”
Read. Search. Read again.
“It fit on a single line.”
The answer. At last.
“The coffee tastes the same. I think.”
The last volume of The Story of Babel.
